newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds surge on U.S., rating news.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds surge on U.S., rating news.

text.p: Argentine bonds rose sharply Tuesday to finish at or near session highs, boosted first by a lower-than-expected U.S. fourth-quarter employment cost index.

Later in the day the whole market benefitted from the decision by Moody's Investors Service to assign a B1 rating to Argentine peso-denominated government bonds. That is the same as the rating on Argentine foreign-currency denominated bonds.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.31 to 125.60, while the FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 3/8 to 89-1/8.
Peso-denominated bonds outperformed the market, gaining the most from the rating news. The peso Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 rose 1.32 pesos to 99.85 in busy trade.
"Many local banks were buying," said a trader.
"The bullish trend is continuing for now," said another.
One sign that the market is on a firm footing was that Argentine bonds maintained their early gains through the session despite a decline in U.S. Treasuries from their early session highs.
Call money rates fell to 5.20 percent from 5.35 percent.
